newsitem.title: CHINA: More than half of Chinese have foreign currencies.
newsitem.headline: More than half of Chinese have foreign currencies.

text.p: About 67.13 percent of China's people hold foreign exchange with their holdings estimated at more than $20 billion, showed a survey published in the Financial News said on Monday.

Nearly half hold onto foreign currency due to fears about a possible devaluation of the domestic yuan currency and about 15.73 percent have the currency to be ready for overseas travel, the newspaper said.
Most Chinese had confidence in the U.S. dollar, with 84.9 percent holding dollars, 35.1 percent holding marks and just 0.7 percent holding Taiwan dollars, it said.
The survey by the Financial Institute under the Bank of China questioned people in Beijing, the north-eastern industrial city of Harbin, in north-western Lanzhou and central Wuhan, it said.
The survey revealed that the rate of foreign currency holdings tended to be influenced by region, income and age, it said.
The rate was about 82.9 percent in Beijing, 66.7 percent in Harbin, 52.3 percent in Wuhan and 45.3 percent in Lanzhou.
The rate for people earning more than 3,000 yuan per month was 100 percent while only 33.3 percent of people with a monthly income of below 300 yuan held foreign currency, it said.
About 88.9 percent of people aged over 60 held foreign currency while the rate for people from 21 to 40 was 69.3 percent, it said.
Most Chinese obtained their foreign currency from swap centres, as gifts from relatives overseas and from working abroad, it said.
